- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

content.text:
Now I have the complete picture. Here is my thorough report.

---

## Project Overview

This is **usememos/memos** (`github.com/usememos/memos`), a Go-based, self-hosted memo/note-taking application. It uses Protocol Buffers for API definitions and supports three database backends: SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL.

## Data Layer Location

The data layer is at:

**`/bench/home/work/store`**

This directory contains:
- Entity type definitions (Go structs) in top-level `.go` files
- The `Driver` interface in `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` defining all persistence operations
- Database driver implementations in `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/`, `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/`, and `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/`
- Database migrations in `/bench/home/work/store/migration/`
- Protobuf-defined sub-types in `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/store/` (used as field types within the Go structs)

## Complete List of Persistent Entity Types

There are **11 persistent entity types** that map to database tables. Each is defined as a Go struct in the `store` package and corresponds to a database table:

| # | Entity Type (Go struct) | Database Table | Definition File | Description |
|---|------------------------|----------------|-----------------|-------------|
| 1 | `User` | `user` | `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` | Application user with role, credentials, profile |
| 2 | `UserSetting` | `user_setting` | `/bench/home/work/store/user_setting.go` | Per-user key-value settings (shortcuts, general prefs, refresh tokens, PATs, webhooks, tags) |
| 3 | `UserIdentity` | `user_identity` | `/bench/home/work/store/user_identity.go` | External identity provider linkage (SSO/OAuth subject to local user mapping) |
| 4 | `Memo` | `memo` | `/bench/home/work/store/memo.go` | Core content entity - a timestamped note/thought |
| 5 | `MemoRelation` | `memo_relation` | `/bench/home/work/store/memo_relation.go` | Relationships between memos (REFERENCE or COMMENT) |
| 6 | `MemoShare` | `memo_share` | `/bench/home/work/store/memo_share.go` | Bearer-token access grants for read-only memo sharing, with optional expiration |
| 7 | `Attachment` | `attachment` | `/bench/home/work/store/attachment.go` | File attachments (images, etc.) linked to memos, stored locally or in S3 |
| 8 | `IdentityProvider` | `idp` | `/bench/home/work/store/idp.go` | OAuth2 identity provider configurations |
| 9 | `Inbox` | `inbox` | `/bench/home/work/store/inbox.go` | User notification inbox items |
| 10 | `Reaction` | `reaction` | `/bench/home/work/store/reaction.go` | Emoji reactions on content (memos) |
| 11 | `InstanceSetting` | `system_setting` | `/bench/home/work/store/instance_setting.go` | Instance-wide configuration settings (basic, general, storage, memo-related, tags, notification, AI) |

### Notes on Historical Tables

Several tables that appeared in earlier migrations have been dropped and no longer exist in the current schema:
- `activity` (dropped in migration 0.27)
- `memo_organizer` (dropped in migration 0.26)
- `webhook` (dropped in migration 0.25, functionality moved to `user_setting`)
- `tag` (dropped in migration 0.22, functionality moved to memo payload)
- `storage` (removed, functionality consolidated into `InstanceSetting`)
- `shortcut` (historical, no longer in current schema)
- `resource` (renamed to `attachment` in migration 0.26)

The `migration_history` table also exists in the database but is infrastructure for tracking schema versions, not a domain entity.

  count=$(grep -rl "store\.${entity}\b" --include='*.go' . | grep -v '^./store/' | grep -v '^./vendor/' | grep -v '^./graphify-out/' | sed 's|^\./||; s|/[^/]*$||' | sort -u | wc -l)
  # Exclude store/* subpackages
  outside=$(grep -rl "store\.${entity}\b" --include='*.go' . | grep -v '^./store/' | grep -v '^./vendor/' | grep -v '^./graphify-out/' | sed 's|^\./||; s|/[^/]*$||' | sort -u | grep -v '^store/' | wc -l)
  pkgs=$(grep -rl "store\.${entity}\b" --include='*.go' . | grep -v '^./store/' | grep -v '^./vendor/' | grep -v '^./graphify-out/' | sed 's|^\./||; s|/[^/]*$||' | sort -u | grep -v '^store/')
  echo "$entity: $outside outside packages — $pkgs"
done

content.text:
h11.

The data layer is the `store/` package (`store/*.go`), which defines 11 persistent entity types. Counting references from packages **outside** that layer:

1. **`User`** — referenced from **~7 packages** outside the store layer (`server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`)
2. **`Memo`** — referenced from **~6 packages** outside the store layer (`server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload`)

The `User` type (defined in `store/user.go`) is the most widely referenced, appearing across authentication, notification, API, file-serving, frontend, and RSS packages. `Memo` (defined in `store/memo.go`) is second, referenced across notification, API, frontend, RSS, and the memo-payload runner. The next closest is `Attachment` at ~4 packages.
